prerequisites: Physics in 2nd year of Bachillerato (high school)
Derivation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed ideal gas systems.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical quantities. Treatment of measurement errors.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First principle of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, a minimum overall score of 2.0 points out of 5.5 for continuous assessment (participation, controls, lab practices) is required. If this minimum is not met, the continuous assessment score will be zero. The final grade (NFO) is calculated as EvC + (1 - EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment score and CGO is the ordinary global exam score. A minimum of 3.5 points (out of 10) is required in the global exam (CGO) for the continuous assessment score to be combined. If the global exam minimum is not reached, or if continuous assessment is lost, the final grade will be the global exam score. A final score below 5.0 results in a FAIL. For extraordinary assessments, continuous assessment scores (EvC) from the ordinary period can be carried over and combined with the extraordinary global exam (CGE) using the same formula, provided a minimum of 3.5 points is obtained in CGE; otherwise, the final score is CGE.
